  excerpt_start_line: 240
  excerpt: Every expressible accepted SMT backend/checker/replay settlement produces one terminal result, never `Tested`;
    no non-`Proved` result carries basis or certification. Negotiation refusals produce no terminal from this map, and neither
    SMT nor Kani map consumes the other backend's outcome.
  type: criterion
- id: FR-034-AC-1
  path: spec/kani/functional/FR-034-caller-death-ownership.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: Before the exclusive caller lease, matching helper identity, verified monitor/INIT/peer, observer re
  excerpt_start_line: 1844
  excerpt: Before the exclusive caller lease, matching helper identity, verified monitor/INIT/peer, observer readiness and
    positive typed Dispatch are established, no production backend instruction is created. Caller SIGKILL, abort or OOM-equivalent
    forced death during initialization may start only bounded guardian bootstrap, which exits without backend on absent lease
    or authorization.
  type: criterion
- id: FR-034-AC-2
  path: spec/kani/functional/FR-034-caller-death-ownership.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: Before any M spawn, O is positively verified outer PID 1 with armed parent-death protection and orig
  excerpt_start_line: 1845
  excerpt: Before any M spawn, O is positively verified outer PID 1 with armed parent-death protection and original-exclusive
    bootstrap authority. Unclaimed inner I is contained by O even if M dies before internal child_wait handoff or startup-info
    reader loss aborts M. Owned outer pidfd termination confirms teardown; missing authority refuses before spawn. No host
    scan, monitor/group exit or successful signal proves cleanup.
  type: criterion
- id: FR-034-AC-3
  path: spec/kani/functional/FR-034-caller-death-ownership.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: In ClaimedBootstrap, InitReady or Dispatched, original-caller lease EOF causes guardian cancellation
  excerpt_start_line: 1846
  excerpt: In ClaimedBootstrap, InitReady or Dispatched, original-caller lease EOF causes guardian cancellation/exit and confirmed
    INIT termination; Dispatched descendants are torn down by the kernel. The test controller observes dead-caller cleanup
    without manufacturing that caller's outcome or evidence.
  type: criterion
- id: FR-034-AC-4
  path: spec/kani/functional/FR-034-caller-death-ownership.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: 'Mutual authority is the specific anonymous connected pair: guardian checks the actual mapped creator'
  excerpt_start_line: 1847
  excerpt: 'Mutual authority is the specific anonymous connected pair: guardian checks the actual mapped creator UID and only
    the original caller holds its executor endpoint. The bounded executor binds kernel credentials of Ready''s actual sender
    to claimed host INIT/start/pidfd/parent/namespace, not socketpair creator credentials alone. Guardian''s creator PID0
    is not a host identity. A foreign actor cannot rebind a public name or supply replacement lease/Dispatch; another pair,
    mismatched UID or replayed authority refuses.'
  type: criterion
- id: FR-034-AC-5
  path: spec/kani/functional/FR-034-caller-death-ownership.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: C retains actual unreaped Child L; L/O/M/I ownership is verified through host pidfds, start/parent/n
  excerpt_start_line: 1848
  excerpt: C retains actual unreaped Child L; L/O/M/I ownership is verified through host pidfds, start/parent/namespace identities
    and actual outer/inner PID 1. O owns actual M Child and I is M's inner child. Reused, stale, incomplete, translated incorrectly
    or dead identity refuses before Dispatch.
  type: criterion
- id: FR-034-AC-6
  path: spec/kani/functional/FR-034-caller-death-ownership.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: 'The owned tree memory observer is ready before typed Dispatch; failed observer preparation releases '
  excerpt_start_line: 1849
  excerpt: The owned tree memory observer is ready before typed Dispatch; failed observer preparation releases no backend
    instruction.
  type: criterion
- id: FR-034-AC-7
  path: spec/kani/functional/FR-034-caller-death-ownership.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: Bounded inner startup/identity recovery is required before Dispatch. M death/reparenting or malforme
  excerpt_start_line: 1850
  excerpt: Bounded inner startup/identity recovery is required before Dispatch. M death/reparenting or malformed/missing info
    cancels through retained outer INIT authority and yields typed setup refusal; complete outer termination is independently
    confirmed. No host scan or gate EOF authorizes a backend.
  type: criterion
- id: FR-034-AC-8
  path: spec/kani/functional/FR-034-caller-death-ownership.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: After Dispatch, original-caller death cancels double-fork/reparented, setsid, late-born and nested-P
  excerpt_start_line: 1851
  excerpt: After Dispatch, original-caller death cancels double-fork/reparented, setsid, late-born and nested-PID-namespace
    descendants through kernel-owned INIT teardown, including descendants absent from previous samples. Observed-PID lists
    or normal-operation host scans are not cancellation authority.
  type: criterion
- id: FR-034-AC-9
  path: spec/kani/functional/FR-034-caller-death-ownership.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: Cancelling one owned namespace leaves concurrent independent runs and unrelated host children unaffe
  excerpt_start_line: 1852
  excerpt: Cancelling one owned namespace leaves concurrent independent runs and unrelated host children unaffected.
  type: criterion
- id: FR-034-AC-10
  path: spec/kani/functional/FR-034-caller-death-ownership.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: Normal backend completion, backend exec failure, explicit cancellation, timeout, memory excess, capt
  excerpt_start_line: 1853
  excerpt: Normal backend completion, backend exec failure, explicit cancellation, timeout, memory excess, capture failure
    and observation failure each require confirmed owned teardown before any proof conclusion. Backend exit or valid success
    output alone never authorizes acceptance.
  type: criterion
- id: FR-034-AC-11
  path: spec/kani/functional/FR-034-caller-death-ownership.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: Guardian SIGKILL, abort or OOM-equivalent death during bootstrap, InitReady or immediately after Dis
  excerpt_start_line: 1854
  excerpt: 'Guardian SIGKILL, abort or OOM-equivalent death during bootstrap, InitReady or immediately after Dispatch cannot
    release an unowned production backend: the guardian is INIT, and its death tears down that namespace. With a live original
    caller, guardian failure always yields a typed refusal and never verified/falsified evidence, even after confirmed teardown
    and beside a valid success report.'
  type: criterion
- id: FR-034-AC-12
  path: spec/kani/functional/FR-034-caller-death-ownership.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: Every startup refusal, completion and cancellation settles actual owned roles before conclusions. An
  excerpt_start_line: 1855
  excerpt: Every startup refusal, completion and cancellation settles actual owned roles before conclusions. Anonymous controls
    and report pipe/memfd have no persistent names and end at final close. All report-owner death reclaims kernel report backing
    without Drop/unlink; other assigned artifacts retain surviving-owner cleanup and truthful all-owner-death limits. No dead
    actor is claimed to reap or unlink.
  type: criterion
- id: FR-034-AC-13
  path: spec/kani/functional/FR-034-caller-death-ownership.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: The bounded executor requires an explicit path to this package's actual Cargo executable quire-kani-
  excerpt_start_line: 1856
  excerpt: The bounded executor requires an explicit path to this package's actual Cargo executable quire-kani-guardian, built
    and supplied with the library from the same package source/build inputs. A missing, non-executable or unusable helper
    gives a typed setup refusal before backend Dispatch, with no PATH/global discovery, copied executable, shell substitute
    or alternate launcher. Cargo library dependency resolution alone is not helper delivery.
  type: criterion
- id: FR-034-AC-14
  path: spec/kani/functional/FR-034-caller-death-ownership.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: Setup docs require the matched package helper roles, safe caller-context user/PID/private-mount perm
  excerpt_start_line: 1857
  excerpt: Setup docs require the matched package helper roles, safe caller-context user/PID/private-mount permissions, verified
    mapping/setgroups/private proc, nested installed bwrap and pidfd/observer facilities. The compiled caller security profile
    is checked, not inferred from binary mode. Caller-profile restriction can refuse runs formerly available through bwrap-only
    permission; ordinary-caller availability requires actual measurement. Missing capability gives typed pre-Dispatch refusal
    without host-policy mutation or weaker mode. Added L/O roles and bounded controls/storage are charged to existing
  excerpt_kind: verbatim_prefix
  type: criterion
- id: FR-034-AC-15
  path: spec/kani/functional/FR-034-caller-death-ownership.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: Typed private controls reject malformed and unknown fields and enforce finite encoded-byte, pending-
  excerpt_start_line: 1858
  excerpt: Typed private controls reject malformed and unknown fields and enforce finite encoded-byte, pending-message and
    startup-work bounds. Ancillary descriptor count/type is exact, received descriptors are CLOEXEC, and unknown/extra/truncated
    ancillary data refuses while closing all received descriptors. Invalid/overlimit control or EOF cancels or refuses rather
    than authorizing Dispatch.
  type: criterion
- id: FR-034-AC-16
  path: spec/kani/functional/FR-034-caller-death-ownership.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: 'Only the original caller holds the pair''s executor endpoint. Guardian receives only its control end '
  excerpt_start_line: 1859
  excerpt: Only the original caller holds the pair's executor endpoint. Guardian receives only its control end as fd0 through
    safe CLOEXEC child-only mapping, borrows it with a safe descriptor API and receives actual backend stdin separately as
    OwnedFd through safe ancillary rights. Backend fd0 restores that original stdin or closed state, while the control/lease
    descriptor is excluded from backend and unrelated exec inheritance. No arbitrary raw-fd adoption or unsafe exception occurs.
  type: criterion
- id: FR-034-AC-17
  path: spec/kani/functional/FR-034-caller-death-ownership.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: Backend receives unchanged raw argument bytes except the explicitly allocated internal report locato
  excerpt_start_line: 1860
  excerpt: 'Backend receives unchanged raw argument bytes except the explicitly allocated internal report locator: harness
    options then -Z unstable-options --export-json /proc/self/fd/N with actual mapped N >=5. Evidence records that exact argv.
    Inherited stdin, inherited/overridden environment and cwd remain unchanged.'
  type: criterion
- id: FR-034-AC-18
  path: spec/kani/functional/FR-034-caller-death-ownership.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: Guardian diagnostics and control use separate channels from backend stdout/stderr captures and canno
  excerpt_start_line: 1861
  excerpt: Guardian diagnostics and control use separate channels from backend stdout/stderr captures and cannot contaminate
    reports; existing bounded capture and capture-failure behavior remain authoritative.
  type: criterion
- id: FR-034-AC-19
  path: spec/kani/functional/FR-034-caller-death-ownership.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: Original identity ceilings and existing outcome classifications remain authoritative after confirmed
  excerpt_start_line: 1862
  excerpt: 'Original identity ceilings and existing outcome classifications remain authoritative after confirmed cleanup:
    memory excess and wall expiry stay distinct, ambiguous live-worker RSS refuses, and ordinary completed/refused/falsified
    reports retain their meanings. Native refinement uses this ownership path when its FR-028 AC-24 typed entry is implemented,
    with unchanged refinement class/evidence rules.'
  type: criterion
- id: FR-034-AC-20
  path: spec/kani/functional/FR-034-caller-death-ownership.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: Guardian connection, startup, identity verification and Dispatch use the original monotonic identity
  excerpt_start_line: 1863
  excerpt: Guardian connection, startup, identity verification and Dispatch use the original monotonic identity deadline without
    resetting it. An already expired deadline causes no Dispatch and settles inconclusive with the timed-out reason as FR-028
    AC-2 states; actual identity-deadline expiry during setup or execution uses the same classification.
  type: criterion
- id: FR-034-AC-21
  path: spec/kani/functional/FR-034-caller-death-ownership.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: Guardian connection and handshake have a finite setup cap within the remaining original deadline. Ca
  excerpt_start_line: 1864
  excerpt: Guardian connection and handshake have a finite setup cap within the remaining original deadline. Cap expiry while
    that deadline remains live is a typed setup refusal, distinct from identity-deadline timeout.
  type: criterion
- id: FR-034-AC-22
  path: spec/kani/functional/FR-034-caller-death-ownership.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: Control/capture shutdown and cleanup observation waits have finite bounds. Unconfirmed termination r

  anchor: Every requested item receives exactly one generated or typed-refused disposition; a refused item con
  excerpt_start_line: 375
  excerpt: Every requested item receives exactly one generated or typed-refused disposition; a refused item contributes no
    function, no environment constructor and no symbol to the generated crate, while its siblings are generated unchanged.
  type: criterion
- id: FR-018-AC-2
  path: spec/oracle/functional/FR-018-composite-equality-oracles.md
  role: examined

  anchor: On every vector of the composite-equality corpus, the generated oracle's `Outcome<bool>`, its admitt
  excerpt_start_line: 376
  excerpt: 'On every vector of the composite-equality corpus, the generated oracle''s `Outcome<bool>`, its admitted charge
    sequence and its consumed counters are equal to those of `quire_contract_runtime::exact::TypeEnvironment::check_equality`
    plus `CheckedEquality::evaluate` invoked directly on an independently constructed environment, operands and fresh `Meter`.
    This criterion claims no agreement with the QSL value authority: that boundary is owned by quire-integration IR-842 (FR-014-AC-47).'
  type: criterion
- id: FR-018-AC-3
  path: spec/oracle/functional/FR-018-composite-equality-oracles.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: Each generated item's claim-map entry records the descriptor the request supplied — operator, both o
  excerpt_start_line: 377
  excerpt: Each generated item's claim-map entry records the descriptor the request supplied — operator, both operand source
    types and both conversion targets — and it is equal to the request's, so the independent native run of AC-2 is driven
    from the request and never read back out of the generated crate.
  type: criterion
- id: FR-018-AC-4
  path: spec/oracle/functional/FR-018-composite-equality-oracles.md
  role: examined

  excerpt_start_line: 378
  excerpt: Each generated item's claim-map entry records an `EqualitySchedule` equal to `CheckedEquality::schedule()` of the
    `CheckedEquality` its descriptor admits, for a top-level text, enum and quantity pair and for each `Plan`-schedule composite
    and collection shape.
  type: criterion
- id: FR-018-AC-5
  path: spec/oracle/functional/FR-018-composite-equality-oracles.md
  role: examined

  anchor: A descriptor with a `convert<T>` operand outside `admits_equality_conversion`, distinct text profile
  excerpt_start_line: 379
  excerpt: A descriptor with a `convert<T>` operand outside `admits_equality_conversion`, distinct text profiles, distinct
    enum declarations, incompatible dimensions, distinct units, or no common type is refused at generation time with its `IllTypedCause`,
    emits no code, and admits no charge on any `Meter`.
  type: criterion
- id: FR-018-AC-6
  path: spec/oracle/functional/FR-018-composite-equality-oracles.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: 'An operand type bearing an IEEE value at any depth — including a `float64` field of a record nested '
  excerpt_start_line: 380
  excerpt: An operand type bearing an IEEE value at any depth — including a `float64` field of a record nested inside a `sequence`
    — is refused as `OperatorIneligible`, and the refusal agrees with `TypeEnvironment::contains_ieee` on the reconstructed
    type at every depth in the corpus.
  type: criterion
- id: FR-018-AC-7
  path: spec/oracle/functional/FR-018-composite-equality-oracles.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: 'On the FR-330 package path, model, function, state and temporal roots outside the equality lowering '
  excerpt_start_line: 381
  excerpt: On the FR-330 package path, model, function, state and temporal roots outside the equality lowering profile retain
    their exact typed `Unsupported` feature-accounting record and source occurrences in `PackageAccounting`; each has its
    own requested key and node tag, no symbol or oracle source, and does not change an independent admitted sibling. A `reference`
    composite rejected by Contract IR's strict reader is a reader-stage `InvalidPackage/InvalidValue` control, not a CG blocker.
    A lowered expression of form `call` is refused as blocked on quire-contract-runtime#34 with no oracle.
  type: criterion
- id: FR-018-AC-8
  path: spec/oracle/functional/FR-018-composite-equality-oracles.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: A declaration closure `TypeEnvironment::new` refuses is refused at generation time carrying that `De
  excerpt_start_line: 382
  excerpt: A declaration closure `TypeEnvironment::new` refuses is refused at generation time carrying that `DeclarationCause`,
    including both recursion passes and a duplicate record field; and each generated oracle calls `TypeEnvironment::check_type`
    on both operand comparison types before `check_equality`, so calling it with an empty environment, one omitting a key
    its operand types reach, or one declaring that closure under a different key, yields `Outcome::Refused(Refusal::CheckedInvariant)`
    with no charge admitted, rather than a panic or a completed Boolean.
  type: criterion
- id: FR-018-AC-9
  path: spec/oracle/functional/FR-018-composite-equality-oracles.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: 'Every generated oracle function returns `Outcome<bool>`, never `bool`: with a denial injected at eac'
  excerpt_start_line: 383
  excerpt: 'Every generated oracle function returns `Outcome<bool>`, never `bool`: with a denial injected at each of `equality.plan-form`,
    `equality.plan`, `equality.pair`, `equality.result-retain` and each conversion charge point in turn, the oracle yields
    `Outcome::Incomplete` naming that point, the denied charge is not applied — every counter equals those of the same run
    stopped immediately before that point — and never a completed Boolean.'
  type: criterion
- id: FR-018-AC-10
  path: spec/oracle/functional/FR-018-composite-equality-oracles.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: Generated bytes are identical across repeated runs and across permutations of the request order, inc
  excerpt_start_line: 384
  excerpt: Generated bytes are identical across repeated runs and across permutations of the request order, including a request
    carrying two descriptors over one node id, and claim-map entries are ordered by the descriptor key — expression node id,
    operator rank, then each operand's source-type and conversion-target node ids, every node id compared in node-id order;
    the generated crate is compiled and executed under AC-2 against a native run driven from the request's own descriptor
    (AC-3), so a generated crate with a changed emitted operator, operand order or descriptor fails AC-2.
  type: criterion

  path: spec/oracle/functional/FR-018-composite-equality-oracles.md
  role: examined

  excerpt_start_line: 385
  excerpt: Every claim marks its operation `caller_declared`, the claim map carries the blocked item "operation identity not
    consumed by codegen's generators", and two items over one node differing only in `EqualityOperator` both generate with
    that mark, under distinct symbols, each built from its own operator's stem, and produce complementary outcomes on a vector
    whose operands differ.
  type: criterion

  excerpt: The generated crate declares `publish = false`, names the Contract Runtime dependency this repository's `Cargo.toml`

    from runtime metering), and compiles.
  type: criterion

  excerpt: Every claim-map entry carries the node id, IR id, package id, source map, claims, reconstructed declaration keys
    and selected schedule of its item, and its declaration keys equal `NodeKey::from_hex` of the V2 node ids its operand types
    reach.
  type: criterion

  path: spec/oracle/functional/FR-018-composite-equality-oracles.md

  excerpt: The `bounded_domain` nodes an operand type reaches (`integer_range`, `rational_range`, `decimal_range`, `text_bounds`,
    `collection_bounds`) are read from `binding` members looked up by name as FR-014 lists them, in any order; a bare literal

  excerpt: 'A `binary` node''s operand is read through its `reference`: a reference to a `convert` expression node is read
    as the type of what it converts, following nested conversions to the first node that is not a conversion, and a reference
    to any other node, including a non-`convert` application, as that node''s own `semantic_type`. A descriptor whose `source_type`
    is the read type generates, and any other source is refused as an operand-type disagreement at that position, reporting
    the read type as found.'

    from that record; it is never relabelled as work exhaustion. When a checked package is admitted under a byte ceiling one
    byte below its otherwise canonical lowered contract package length, Contract IR FR-038-AC-95 returns `Failed(Bytes)` for
    every requested root with that ceiling as `limit` and one shared `consumed` above it, and exposes neither canonical package

  excerpt: For every item of the TC-029 corpus whose leaves are Boolean or bounded integers, the claim-map closure's member
    names, presence and each integer leaf's inclusive bounds equal those of an independent read of the checked package (the
    V2 composite and `bounded_domain` nodes read through Contract IR's reader, never through the generator's reconstruction);

  excerpt: Type reconstruction of QSpec's `positive-recursive-records.json` List (through `Option<List>`) and Tree (through
    `Sequence<Tree>` bounded `[0,3]`) closes each back-edge at the in-progress record key, generates equality items built
    over both record types, and terminates; a synthetic unclosed `Option` self-cycle and a `Sequence` self-cycle each refuse
    as `TypeResolutionCycle` naming the repeated type node, without a panic, stack overflow or generated symbol. PLANNED (IR-643).
  type: criterion

  anchor: The per-item type-resolution counter charges one unit for each root type-node entry or followed type
  excerpt_start_line: 399
  excerpt: 'The per-item type-resolution counter charges one unit for each root type-node entry or followed type-node reference
    or bounded-domain `semantic_type` edge, including a repeated or memoized reference, across both operands and conversion
    targets, independently of Contract IR lowering; with the default limit, an acyclic chain reaches its 65,537th entry and
    refuses only its item as `TypeResolutionWorkExhausted { limit: 65_536, consumed: 65_537 }` before further descent and
    without call-stack exhaustion or generated symbols, while a sibling needing at most 65,536 entries still generates. PLANNED
    (I'
  excerpt_kind: verbatim_prefix
  type: criterion

  role: examined

  anchor: Reading the QSpec List `next` field as `binding(next, aggregate([binding(optional, reference Option<
  excerpt_start_line: 400
  excerpt: Reading the QSpec List `next` field as `binding(next, aggregate([binding(optional, reference Option<List>)]))`
    yields exactly one `FieldDeclaration` named `next`, with `Presence::Optional` and payload type `ValueType::Composite(List
    NodeKey)`; removing or renaming `optional`, adding a second nested member, or targeting a non-option node refuses only
    that item as malformed, never as a required field or a generated oracle. PLANNED (IR-643).
  type: criterion
- id: FR-018-AC-27
  path: spec/oracle/functional/FR-018-composite-equality-oracles.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: Reading the QSpec Tree `kids` field's direct reference to `collection_bounds` follows that node's `s
  excerpt_start_line: 401
  excerpt: Reading the QSpec Tree `kids` field's direct reference to `collection_bounds` follows that node's `semantic_type`
    to `Sequence<Tree>`, reads its sole element reference as the Tree `NodeKey`, and reconstructs cardinality `[0,3]` from
    that bound node's named `min` and `max`; changing the semantic type to a non-sequence, dropping or duplicating either
    bound, or making either value non-integer refuses only that item with a typed cause and emits no code, never silently
    yielding an unbounded collection. PLANNED (IR-643).
  type: criterion
- id: FR-018-AC-28
  path: spec/oracle/functional/FR-018-composite-equality-oracles.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: With a caller-selected type-resolution work limit of at least 100,000 and `cg.equality.source_bytes`
  excerpt_start_line: 402
  excerpt: With a caller-selected type-resolution work limit of at least 100,000 and `cg.equality.source_bytes` raised to
    the measured flat source size, an admitted acyclic type chain of 100,000 entries reconstructs and generates an oracle
    with the same result as an equivalent shallow type on a 512 KiB stack; with the same raised source-byte limit, the default
    type-resolution work limit refuses it at entry 65,537, and a selected work limit one below its entry count refuses it
    at the first denied entry. No depth setting or fixed depth refusal participates in these runs. PLANNED (IR-511).
  type: criterion

  excerpt_start_line: 403
  excerpt: A cycle detected after a charged repeated entry reports `TypeResolutionCycle` without following a child; if that
    repeated entry is the first denied work entry, `TypeResolutionWorkExhausted` wins and reports the effective limit and
    first denied count. An unaffected sibling keeps its original disposition in either case. PLANNED (IR-511).
  type: criterion
- id: FR-018-AC-30

  excerpt_start_line: 404
  excerpt: The 100,000-entry acyclic closure renders as flat source without a type-depth-sized constructor expression; under
    the 1,048,576-byte default it returns `SourceTooLarge` naming that limit when the source exceeds it, and under a caller
    limit equal to its measured source bytes it emits a complete, compilable oracle within the publication artifact and bundle
    byte limits. One byte less refuses before that byte is appended and publishes no partial artifact. PLANNED (IR-511).
  type: criterion

  path: spec/oracle/functional/FR-018-composite-equality-oracles.md

    or charging; with `u64::MAX - 1`, the first denied count fits in the `u64` `consumed` field and is reported without wraparound.

  excerpt_start_line: 406
  excerpt: Each IR-admitted direct `temporal`/`formula`, `temporal`/`fairness` and `expression`/`case` request has one claim-map
    entry keyed by its requested node id and refused as `CompositeEqualityRefusal::Unsupported`. For an IR `Unsupported` lowering
    record, the refusal's `unsupported_node_id` and `node_tag` equal that record's first unsupported reachable node and tag,
    which need not be the requested root; for a lowered `case` root they name the root and `"expression"`. The request contributes
    no generated symbol or source, never panics or disappears, and leaves a supported sibling's claim and source
  excerpt_kind: verbatim_prefix
  type: criterion

  excerpt: 'For each function-application corpus vector, the oracle''s outcome, admitted charge sequence and consumed counters

    Contract Runtime `exact` port (historical), and CG names no QSL application API as its replacement (IR-845). This criterion
    claims no agreement with the QSL value authority: that boundary is owned by quire-integration IR-842 (FR-014-AC-47, FR-021-AC-18).
    PLANNED, blocked on IR-853: once Contract Runtime FR-275 deletes the `exact` port, this criterion''s comparison ta'

  excerpt: Each scheduled item records the requested function name and declaring V2 function node id, plus its request-order

  excerpt_start_line: 251
  excerpt: 'The oracle returns the arity, wrong-value-kind, dangling-reference and unknown-function input refusals unchanged
    to the caller before any execution charge; the schedule records ordered arguments without inventing a refusal result.
    That the refusals equal QSL-owned ones is outside CG''s boundary (IR-842, FR-014-AC-47). PLANNED, blocked on IR-853: once
    Contract Runtime FR-275 deletes the `exact` port, the refusal comparison''s target is decided by IR-853.'

  excerpt_start_line: 252
  excerpt: 'The schedule orders arity validation before per-argument validation, validates arguments in declared parameter

    The corpus half is PLANNED, blocked on IR-853: once Contract Runtime FR-275 deletes the `exact` port, its target is decided

  excerpt_start_line: 270

  excerpt_start_line: 271
  excerpt: 'Items on one `call` node, with equal argument operands, that name functions absent from the request''s declarations
    each get their own claim-map entry. Requesting `zz_unknown` and `aa_unknown` on one node yields two entries, in that order:
    `UnknownFunction { name: "aa_unknown" }`, then `UnknownFunction { name: "zz_unknown" }` (function name compared byte-wise
    over its UTF-8 bytes, case-sensitively), and no `DuplicateRequest`; the entries are identical under both request orders.
    Requesting `Zz_unknown` and `aa_unknown` yields `Zz_unknown` first, because `Z` (0x5A) sorts before `a` (0x61). Reques'
  excerpt_kind: verbatim_prefix

  path: spec/oracle/functional/FR-021-function-application-oracles.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: Across one body, the counter charges each node entry, child edge, emitted instruction and location r
  excerpt_start_line: 272
  excerpt: 'Across one body, the counter charges each node entry, child edge, emitted instruction and location record once
    in source traversal order. A setting equal to the required units emits a complete schedule; one less refuses that function
    as `GenerationWorkExhausted { limit, consumed: limit + 1 }` before the denied action, with no partial root or location
    record and no change to an unrelated function. A failed Contract IR lowering record keeps its lowering refusal and incurs
    no generation charge. PLANNED (IR-511).'
  type: criterion

  anchor: The target-neutral schedule's branch/stop edges order a denied left-operand charge to stop before th
  excerpt_start_line: 273
  excerpt: The target-neutral schedule's branch/stop edges order a denied left-operand charge to stop before the right operand
    charge, and, after the left completes, the right charge before the parent operation. Owner-path execution matching an
    equivalent shallow body is outside CG's boundary (IR-845).
  type: criterion

  excerpt_start_line: 274
  excerpt: An admitted nested body consists of separate V2 expression nodes connected only by `reference` leaves under QSpec
    FR-322, with each expression node reached from one parent in this CG subset; callee argument 0 binds an exact V2 function
    node, parameter references bind the declared parameter slots, and remaining arguments preserve source order. Missing,
    cyclic, shared-expression, unbound-parameter, ill-typed or wrong-operation edges refuse with a typed cause before schedule
    emission. PLANNED (IR-511).
  type: criterion

  excerpt_start_line: 275
  excerpt: Under the default 1,048,576-byte source limit, a 100,000-instruction body that needs more bytes returns `SourceTooLarge`
    naming the default; raising the caller limit to its measured flat source bytes emits a complete compilable schedule crate,
    with deterministic ordinal-range modules if one artifact would exceed its publication limit. One byte below the measured
    count refuses before append with no partial output. PLANNED (IR-511).
  type: criterion

  excerpt_start_line: 276
  excerpt: A 100,000-call linear body produces 100,000 constant-size parent-linked location records; requesting its deepest
    path under sufficient query limits returns exactly 100,000 child ordinals, and a one-unit-below query limit refuses without
    a partial path. Generation does not materialize all paths. PLANNED (IR-511).
  type: criterion

  excerpt_start_line: 277
  excerpt: A requested generation work limit of `u64::MAX` returns `InvalidGenerationWorkLimit` before lowering or charging;
    at `u64::MAX - 1` the first denied count is representable in the `u64` refusal and never wraps or panics. PLANNED (IR-511).

  excerpt: 'IMPLEMENTED (IR-596). Under a `reject` integer type, an add, subtract or multiply result outside the type''s interval

    returns a wrapped value, and no case returns the refusal.'

    both inclusive domain endpoints fit i64. A minimum of `i64::MIN - 1` or `i128::MIN`, or a maximum of `i64::MAX + 1` or
    `i128::MAX`, produces `UnsupportedExpression` at the first affected expression source span and no generated source; the
    same rule applies to an out-of-range literal. Values are never narrowed, clamped or wrapped to create an oracle.

  excerpt: For each of the six profiles and both `Text[0,8]` and `Text[1,1]`, a real Kani harness symbolically ranges over
    all 21 sequences of zero to two scalars from the four-scalar alphabet, constructs each `TextPayload` by `from_utf8`, compares

  excerpt_start_line: 360

    with cause `Verdicts` (`violation` proved, `success` replayed). The envelope is on the `Witness` arm with a payload `witness`

  excerpt: 'The normative Kani form set is the complete V1 proof set defined by IR-269 and FR-015: scalar families Boolean,
    integer, rational, decimal, IEEE float, text, enum and quantity; record and tuple composite equality; function application;
    precondition, postcondition and invariant `BoundClause` roles; and bounded collection and graph forms. V1 `ClauseKind`
    has no frame variant. State before/after and frame obligations are typed V2 `StateFrame` items with the `contract` or
    `frame` role, included where FR-015 defines their typed lowering. Each item is identified by its typed IR tag/form, family,
    ope'
  excerpt_kind: verbatim_prefix

  excerpt_start_line: 558

  excerpt_start_line: 560

  excerpt_start_line: 561

    SMT arm under its applicable EN-2 or EN-3 method. HP-4 and an unadvertised HP form settle unsupported before an engine,

  excerpt_start_line: 562

  excerpt_start_line: 563
  excerpt: PLANNED (IR-516). A selected reduction reaches only a candidate advertising that exact reduction, with the selection
    preserved in the routed request. Symmetry declarations and POR enter the obligation identity, so their reduced and unreduced
    requests for one claim have distinct obligation identities; a state constraint changes request identity but leaves obligation
    identity unchanged. An unadvertised selection or POR on a subject with no footprints settles `unsupported` without an
    artifact, and no arm drops or adds a reduction.
  type: criterion

  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md

  excerpt_start_line: 564
  excerpt: PLANNED (IR-516). For an item over a weak `parallel`, a candidate advertising the subject's resolved `tso` or `ra`
    model receives that exact model; a candidate lacking it settles `unsupported` with no artifact, and no arm weakens the
    resolved model. An `sc` subject is a separate strong-model control and does not take the weak-memory branch.
  type: criterion

  excerpt: PLANNED (IR-516). With otherwise equal form and kind advertisement, model and protocol subject classes are read
    separately; an arm that discharges only one class settles the other `unsupported`, while a supported protocol item retains
    its protocol transition-system subject identity through routing.

  excerpt_start_line: 566

    `numeric.narrow` occurrences in one admitted ContractPackage settle independently under the same Kani descriptor. Each
    preflight result is classified from its own selected result context; changing the selected narrow changes that item's
    typed result identity or refusal without changing the other. A node-only classifier or package-wide choice of either bound
    fails this control.
  type: criterion

  excerpt: For a V2 scalar claim, an absent `OwnResult`, an application occurrence absent from the admitted source, a conversion
    occurrence from another source or unrelated to the application, a missing conversion context root, or a ContractPackage
    source identity different from the checked source settles `invalid-request` with a typed form/context cause and no artifact
    or harness. Request and candidate/manifest defects retain their earlier precedence; for a valid candidate this selected-form
    refusal precedes extent and advertised-mode refusal. Neither a source message nor a caller maximum repairs the se

  excerpt_start_line: 336
  excerpt: Generation dispatches one arm per variant of the closed `BackendKind` through an exhaustive `match` with no catch-all,
    and `GenerationContexts::has` handles each variant; adding a variant without either arm does not compile. `Process` requires
    no context.
  type: criterion

  excerpt_start_line: 337
  excerpt: For a set of routed Kani items, each record and harness in the output equals what `negotiate_kani_obligations`
    returns for the same items in ascending request-index order with the same context. The one difference is that every index
    inside a record is the driver's request index, and each harness is paired with the record whose `harness_symbol` names
    it.
  type: criterion

  excerpt: A Kani group-level refusal (for example an unwind outside `1..=1024`, or an unparsable subject path) is returned

  excerpt_start_line: 342
  excerpt: A Kani group containing an `invalid_request` item is listed in `rejected`, and every Kani item's record is returned
    with no harness. A `DuplicateItem` reported by FR-015 has `first_index` rewritten to the driver's request index of the
    first occurrence. On the FR-330 package path, an identical selected scalar occurrence pair also retains FR-039's earlier
    typed `DuplicateRequest` claim refusal at both positions.

  excerpt_start_line: 343
  excerpt: Every routed item appears exactly once in `items`, in ascending request index, under its routed backend and the
    `KindOutput` variant of its routed kind. An item the arm refuses at lowering keeps its typed FR-015 refusal and no harness.
    An empty routed set returns an empty result.
  type: criterion

  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-022-routed-generation.md

  excerpt_start_line: 344
  excerpt: Regeneration from equal inputs is byte-identical, and a permutation of the routed-item slice yields an identical
    result. The same node routed at a different request index or under another candidate of the same backend yields a byte-identical
    harness when the admitted FR-330 package and selected occurrence are the same.
  type: criterion

  anchor: The Kani arm derives each item's operation and domain from the package alone; the caller supplies no
  excerpt_start_line: 345
  excerpt: The Kani arm derives each item's operation and domain from the package alone; the caller supplies no claim map,

  excerpt_start_line: 346
  excerpt: 'An item with no derivable descriptor keeps its typed refusal and no harness, and its siblings'' records and harnesses
    are unaffected. On the FR-330 package path, an absent root retains its exact admitted `InvalidInput` accounting and `PackageRefused`
    output before Kani. On a direct FR-015 request, a node absent from the graph is `invalid_request` and rejects the group.
    A node that does not lower or has a refused bound keeps the FR-015 disposition it has when its claim is generated by FR-014
    (`requires_bound`, `blocked_on_upstream`, `unsatisfiable_bound`). A repeated selected pair on the FR-330 '
  excerpt_kind: verbatim_prefix
  type: criterion

  excerpt: '`RoutedGeneration.claim_map` is `Some` after a Kani group and contains one claim per selected node/occurrence
    admitted past FR-039 accounting, retaining any earlier typed `DuplicateRequest` refusal; an underivable node has one refused
    claim of provenance `underived`, ordered by node id and then selected occurrence key.'

  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: The Kani arm routes an integer node over bounded parameters to a supported harness whose arguments a
  excerpt_start_line: 348
  excerpt: 'The Kani arm routes an integer node over bounded parameters to a supported harness whose arguments are one range
    per operand and whose result assertion uses the result bound: `a + b` over `[0, 9]` and `[10, 20]` with result `[0, 29]`
    has arguments `[0, 9]` and `[10, 20]`; `-e` over `[1, 9]` with result `[-9, -1]` and `e * f` over `[1, 9]` and `[100,
    200]` with result `[100, 1800]` are supported; a node with a plain-typed `reference` operand beside bounded typing (FR-014-AC-25)
    settles `requires_bound` and has no harness.'
  type: criterion

  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-022-routed-generation.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e

  excerpt_start_line: 349
  excerpt: '`RoutedGeneration.oracle_artifacts` is `Some` after a Kani group and `None` when nothing is routed. Its `claim-map.json`
    equals the complete package-derived claim map, including typed refused items; a group with no generated claim still returns
    its crate. For `x + 1` over a parameter `Int[0, 9]`, each `Generated` claim''s oracle symbol is defined in the returned
    `src/lib.rs` and appears in the supported harness''s Rust source.'

  excerpt_start_line: 350
  excerpt: 'The Kani arm routes the packages QSL emits for `x + 1` over `x: Int[0, 9]` into `Int[0, 10]`, `x + y` over `Int[0,
    9]` and `Int[10, 20]` into `Int[10, 29]`, and `-z` over `Int[0, 9]` into `Int[-9, 0]` (a literal as a reference to its
    own `value` node, the declared bound on a narrowing `conversion` consuming the plain-typed arithmetic node) to supported
    harnesses with arguments `[0, 9]` and `[1, 1]`; `[0, 9]` and `[10, 20]`; and `[0, 9]`, each asserting the result against
    the conversion''s bound (`[0, 10]`, `[10, 29]`, `[-9, 0]`). In that shape a plain-Integer parameter beside a bounded one,
    and'
  excerpt_kind: verbatim_prefix
  type: criterion

  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-022-routed-generation.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e

  excerpt_start_line: 351
  excerpt: Two Kani harnesses with one `harness_symbol` refuse the call as `DuplicateHarness` naming the second harness's
    `module::harness` path, and no harness is overwritten or dropped.

  excerpt_start_line: 352
  excerpt: PLANNED (IR-629). A routed `Process(id)` item appears exactly once with its own identity and empty `KindOutput::Process`,

  excerpt_start_line: 353
  excerpt: PLANNED (IR-629). A crate-internal routed `Process(id)` item whose private backend and kind disagree refuses the

  excerpt_start_line: 354
  excerpt: PLANNED (IR-629). Permuting a routed-item slice containing Kani and multiple process identities leaves its request-index-ordered
    output unchanged.

  excerpt_start_line: 355
  excerpt: PLANNED (IR-629). `RoutedGenerationItem.backend` and `.kind` are private while `request_index` and `node_id` remain
    public; external callers cannot create an item with a hand-built `Process(id)` or reassign its backend after `from_descriptor`
    construction.

  excerpt_start_line: 356
  excerpt: PLANNED (IR-629). `from_descriptor` constructs Kani for a linked `kani` descriptor and `Process(id)` for a process
    descriptor with the same identity text. An unknown linked identity never produces Process.
  type: criterion

  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-022-routed-generation.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: PLANNED (IR-629). `from_descriptor` rejects a backend identity different from the descriptor identit
  excerpt_start_line: 357
  excerpt: PLANNED (IR-629). `from_descriptor` rejects a backend identity different from the descriptor identity as `DescriptorBackendMismatch`,
    naming both; it rejects an unknown linked identity as `UnknownLinkedBackend`, naming the backend. Neither refusal produces
    a routed item.
  type: criterion
- id: FR-022-AC-23
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-022-routed-generation.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: After FR-019 authenticates two `integer.add` driver items on one admitted ContractPackage with disti
  excerpt_start_line: 358
  excerpt: After FR-019 authenticates two `integer.add` driver items on one admitted ContractPackage with distinct selected
    application/direct-`numeric.narrow` pairs, routed generation retains the pair for each item in its claim and harness identity
    and asserts against its own selected result bound. The two generated harnesses have distinct identities and expected ranges;
    a fresh settlement of a changed selection changes or refuses only that item, without borrowing the other bound.
  type: criterion
- id: FR-022-AC-24
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-022-routed-generation.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: A routed scalar item's retained authenticated selection and its driver lowering position must name t
  excerpt_start_line: 359
  excerpt: A routed scalar item's retained authenticated selection and its driver lowering position must name the same application/conversion
    pair in the same admitted ContractPackage. A changed pair, missing conversion context root or occurrence absent from that
    package refuses the whole call with a typed selection error before any harness. No package-wide bound search, source-text
    reparse or copied QSL context supplies a replacement.
  type: criterion
- id: FR-022-AC-25
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-022-routed-generation.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: The public CG API exposes the concrete `ContractScalarError` carried by `RoutedGenerationError::Cont
  excerpt_start_line: 360
  excerpt: The public CG API exposes the concrete `ContractScalarError` carried by `RoutedGenerationError::ContractScalar`,
    so an external driver can match `ContractScalarError::Oracle(OracleGenerationError::SourceTooLarge { bytes, limit, setting
    })` and distinguish the scalar source ceiling from request-accounting and other oracle failures without parsing text or
    naming a private module.
  type: criterion
- id: FR-022-AC-26
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-022-routed-generation.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: Given the checked QSL RR-16 package with two `x + 1` occurrences of one application node, directly n
  excerpt_start_line: 361
  excerpt: Given the checked QSL RR-16 package with two `x + 1` occurrences of one application node, directly narrowed to
    `Int[0, 10]` and `Int[0, 20]`, the driver supplies two distinct request indexes and occurrence keys. CG matches each to
    its own requirement record and selected narrow; both supported scalar outputs use the shared application operation and
    their respective result bounds, and their obligation and harness identities differ by application occurrence. Reversing
    routed-item order leaves these pairings unchanged.
  type: criterion
- id: FR-022-AC-27
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-022-routed-generation.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: For `if p then x + 1 else x + 1`, each occurrence's generated scalar claim is conditional on its own
  excerpt_start_line: 362
  excerpt: 'For `if p then x + 1 else x + 1`, each occurrence''s generated scalar claim is conditional on its own QSL path
    guard: the same guard occurrence with `holds=true` for the then item and `holds=false` for the else item. CG preserves
    the full outermost-first guard sequence and uses it when forming the proof obligation; a result under `p=false` cannot
    prove the then claim and one under `p=true` cannot prove the else claim. An empty path condition remains unguarded.'
  type: criterion
- id: FR-022-AC-28
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-022-routed-generation.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: If a routed scalar item's occurrence has no entry in the supplied requirement records, its key's nod
  excerpt_start_line: 363
  excerpt: If a routed scalar item's occurrence has no entry in the supplied requirement records, its key's node disagrees
    with the authenticated application selection, or the keyed record disagrees with the item's result bound, direct conversion
    occurrence or ordered path condition, CG returns a typed refusal identifying the request index and occurrence before emitting
    an oracle, harness or obligation identity for that request; it does not use another record with the same node or reconstruct
    missing values from the IR graph or source text.
  type: criterion
- id: FR-022-AC-29
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-022-routed-generation.md
  role: examined
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: Given an admitted package whose complete lowering sequence has bound driver items at indexes 0 and 2
  excerpt_start_line: 364
  excerpt: 'Given an admitted package whose complete lowering sequence has bound driver items at indexes 0 and 2 and an excluded
    accounting-only position at index 1, a routed item with `request_index` 1 and the excluded position''s exact `node_id`
    refuses the whole call as `ExcludedDriverIndex { request_index: 1, node_id }` before any generation arm, oracle or harness.
    The same routed backend and descriptor at indexes 0 and 2 remain valid controls, and CG never substitutes an envelope
    position or the next bound item''s selection for index 1.'
  type: criterion

- id: FR-002-AC-2
  path: spec/strategy/functional/FR-002-tristate-proptest.md
  role: examined

    from that node. For a grouped node, it shall supply an

    `ApplicationIdentityContext` made from the complete, ordered draft graph. The

    builder shall use the resulting candidate node ID for fixture assembly and

    retain the checked-package reader as the admission authority. It shall not

    construct or hash a local copy of the application preimage or its version tag.


    '

    \ but "

  role: context_only
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: When the driver submits a complete-V1 request for production negotiation or
  excerpt_start_line: 29
  excerpt: 'When the driver submits a complete-V1 request for production negotiation or

    generation, this generator SHALL base every decision about its selected IR

    meaning on the one admitted QSpec FR-330 `ContractPackage` emitted for that

    request. Contract IR owns its lowering and sole strict reader; CG consumes the

    typed admitted value and does not define another package schema or reader.


    This requirement governs the production oracle and Kani paths, including the

    [FR-019](../../routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md) settlement

    and [FR-022](../../routed/functional/FR-022-routed-generation.md'
  excerpt_kind: verbatim_prefix
  type: FR

    oracles FR-014 generated, the code generator shall emit one bounded Kani

    obligation per precondition, postcondition, invariant and frame condition,

    and every item it lowers is a claim over an admitted `quire.checked-package/v2`

    package.


    For production requests after the FR-330 consumer transition,

    [FR-039](../../core/functional/FR-039-contract-package-consump'

  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: When a caller runs an FR-015, FR-022/FR-014 or FR-035 harness, the code generator shall invoke the
  excerpt_start_line: 23
  excerpt: 'When a caller runs an FR-015, FR-022/FR-014 or FR-035 harness, the code generator shall invoke the

    installed Kani backend and retain the backend''s own reported outcome as typed

    execution evidence. A caller may hand the generator several harnesses to run together

    (FR-017-AC-21 to FR-017-AC-25); the generator then forms groups, runs each

    group in one launcher process, and retains one evidence record per harness. Unless a

    statement says "batch" or "group", it describes a run of one harness.


    [FR-040](./FR-040-cancellation-producer.md) adds the one launcher-observed cancellation outcome:

    the backe'

  path: spec/kani/functional/FR-025-generated-subject-abi.md
  role: context_only
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: When the code generator emits an [FR-015](./FR-015-bounded-kani-obligations.md) harness, it shall
  excerpt_start_line: 21
  excerpt: 'When the code generator emits an [FR-015](./FR-015-bounded-kani-obligations.md) harness, it shall

    emit the harness''s symbolic arguments in the order of the obligation identity''s `arguments`, which

    ascend by identifier. Each argument binding names its parameter node id and declared domain, each

    argument has the Rust type its family''s row below states, and each argument reaches the generated

    oracle widened into the complete-V1 value type without loss.


    The ascending order, the binding to a parameter node id and declared domain, and lossless widening

    are what AD-016 arrow 5 and QSL ADR-013 O-25 d'
  excerpt_kind: verbatim_prefix

- id: FR-028
  path: spec/kani/functional/FR-028-bounded-proof-ceilings.md
  role: context_only
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: 'The code generator shall bound every Kani harness so that its run can finish: each harness identity'
  excerpt_start_line: 25
  excerpt: 'The code generator shall bound every Kani harness so that its run can finish: each harness identity

    records a memory ceiling and a wall-clock ceiling, a run that exceeds either settles `inconclusive`

    with its own reason, and the evidence records the bounds and ceilings the run used. Proof coverage

    is maximised per family. A family proves the production code where its harness verifies within the

    ceilings, and a bounded shadow together with a refinement obligation where it does not

    ([ADR-003](../../decisions/ADR-003-kani-tractability.md)).


    Planned (IR-241): ADR-003 decides that a shadow exists '
  excerpt_kind: verbatim_prefix
  type: FR

  anchor: The Kani adapter shall map every `KaniRunOutcome`, with its inconclusive reason or typed
  excerpt_start_line: 25
  excerpt: 'The Kani adapter shall map every `KaniRunOutcome`, with its inconclusive reason or typed

    cancellation source, paired with the settlement of that run''s replay, to QSL''s FR-331 terminal

    value (`qsl_replay::TerminalValue`) in

    one match with no catch-all arm ([ADR-002](../../decisions/ADR-002-backend-adapter-boundary.md)

    Q3). The map is total over the pair (outcome, replay settlement), not over the outcome alone: a

    falsified run''s value is a function of both, because a counterexample is a refutation only once its

    replay reproduces it. Every pair maps to exactly one terminal value, so every run ite'
  excerpt_kind: verbatim_prefix
  type: FR

  path: spec/kani/functional/FR-030-ir-outcome-terminal-map.md
  role: context_only
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: The generator shall map every Contract IR `KaniOutcome`, paired with the settlement of its replay, t
  excerpt_start_line: 27
  excerpt: 'The generator shall map every Contract IR `KaniOutcome`, paired with the settlement of its replay, to

    exactly one `qsl_replay::TerminalValue`. The map is total over the pair (outcome, replay

    settlement), not over the outcome alone, and it preserves the outcome''s refusal cause: the outcome

    kinds that QSL''s terminal value collapses into one variant stay distinguishable through that

    variant''s typed cause. This is QSL ADR-013 C-09 as merged, whose two inputs are the IR `KaniOutcome`

    and, for a `Counterexample`, the result of its replay. The replay settlement, its six readings and

    the rules that cl'
  excerpt_kind: verbatim_prefix
  type: FR

  excerpt_start_line: 17

    [FR-028](./FR-028-bounded-proof-ceilings.md) AC-21 retains its resource authority. The preceding

    does not depend on completing all parent IR-241 work, which IR-639 itself blocks.


    Planned CODE: the selected IR-652 allocation adds '

  role: context_only
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e

  excerpt_start_line: 21
  excerpt: 'When a caller requests cancellation of a bounded Kani execution, the generator SHALL observe the

    caller-owned `quire_exact::Cancel` handle at the real launcher and retain the cause of the first

    cancellation event that stops that launcher. The caller owns the handle and any timer: a timer can

    call `cancel(CancelCause::Deadline)`, while an elapsed [FR-028](./FR-028-bounded-proof-ceilings.md)

    execution ceiling without a recorded cancellation event remains `TimedOut`. This requirement adds

    one producer path to [FR-017](./FR-017-kani-execution-evidence.md); it does not treat a Contract IR

    outcome r'
  excerpt_kind: verbatim_prefix
  type: FR
- id: FR-041

  role: context_only
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: When the repository claims proof coverage for a generated-harness module, its existing
  excerpt_start_line: 17
  excerpt: 'When the repository claims proof coverage for a generated-harness module, its existing

    [`make kani-gate`](../non-functional/NFR-006-real-kani-lane-gating.md) SHALL accept that claim only

    after a real Kani run discharges a proposition in the module and an executed mutation inside the

    module falsifies a proof check. The gate applies the proof-stage acceptance rule of QSL ADR-011

    §2.3 to CG''s claimed modules. It makes no claim about a module absent from its declared list or

    about a semantic stage the test input did not traverse.'
  type: FR

  excerpt_start_line: 25
  excerpt: 'When a caller supplies an admitted `quire.checked-package/v2` package and a set

    of equality expression nodes, the code generator shall emit a deterministic Rust

    oracle crate whose functions decide each node by reconstructing the item''s

    `TypeEnvironment` and calling the Contract Runtime

    `TypeEnvironment::check_equality` and `CheckedEquality::evaluate` with a

    caller-supplied `Meter`. It never compares two values structurally, and never

    copies a resource charge or a planned pair count.


    This is the composite/structural equality slice of complete-V1 oracle

    generation. [FR-014](./FR-014-exact-scala'
  excerpt_kind: verbatim_prefix
  type: FR
- id: FR-021
  path: spec/oracle/functional/FR-021-function-application-oracles.md
  role: context_only
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: When a caller supplies an admitted `quire.checked-package/v2` package, function
  excerpt_start_line: 29
  excerpt: 'When a caller supplies an admitted `quire.checked-package/v2` package, function

    bindings and requested `call` nodes, the generator shall classify the admitted

    expression-node graph, build a deterministic, target-neutral instruction

    schedule for each admitted body, and record one generated or typed-refused

    disposition per item. The schedule preserves V2 operation identity, operand

    order, value/result types, function binding, and source occurrence identity;

    it states no charge amount and executes no operation itself. Its body analysis

    and schedule emission use charged iterative walks and no fixe'
  excerpt_kind: verbatim_prefix
  type: FR
- id: FR-031
  path: spec/oracle/functional/FR-031-boolean-oracle-integer-arithmetic.md
  role: context_only
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: The Boolean oracle of `interface-001`'s `oracle_slice` lowers one validated Boolean clause over
  excerpt_start_line: 31
  excerpt: 'The Boolean oracle of `interface-001`''s `oracle_slice` lowers one validated Boolean clause over

    Boolean and bounded-integer values into a Rust function. Its clauses may hold integer add,

    subtract, multiply, divide and remainder, and the six integer comparisons. Today the emitter

    renders each of those five operators as the raw Rust infix operator on `i64`, and each comparison

    as the raw infix comparison. It never reads the operand type''s overflow policy. On overflow the

    generated function panics in a debug build and wraps in a release build, and on a zero divisor it

    panics. The exact kernel''s i'
  excerpt_kind: verbatim_prefix
  type: FR
- id: FR-035
  path: spec/oracle/functional/FR-035-caller-text-admission.md
  role: context_only
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: When a caller requests runtime Text admission, the code generator shall emit an
  excerpt_start_line: 17
  excerpt: 'When a caller requests runtime Text admission, the code generator shall emit an

    oracle and a separately bounded Kani obligation for a caller-owned

    `TextPayload` and declared `TextType`. This is a caller-ingress claim, not a

    claim about an expression node in an admitted `CheckedPackageV2`. The oracle

    calls the exact kernel''s `quire_exact::admit_text` API and returns its

    outcome and metering unchanged. Its evidence identifies the caller-declared

    profile, inclusive length bounds, payload class and proof configuration,

    without `ir_confirmed` provenance, a checked node id or a QSL term identity.


    I'
  excerpt_kind: verbatim_prefix
  type: FR
- id: FR-042
  path: spec/oracle/functional/FR-042-generated-checked-invariant-causes.md
  role: context_only
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: The code generator SHALL assign the shared quire-exact typed checked-invariant cause at each generat
  excerpt_start_line: 13
  excerpt: The code generator SHALL assign the shared quire-exact typed checked-invariant cause at each generated Boolean,
    equality, function and pre-check placeholder constructor.
  type: FR
- id: FR-016
  path: spec/replay/functional/FR-016-witness-native-replay.md
  role: context_only
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: When a FR-015 harness yields a counterexample, the code generator shall decode
  excerpt_start_line: 21
  excerpt: 'When a FR-015 harness yields a counterexample, the code generator shall decode

    the witness into typed complete-V1 values, validate each value against its

    declared domain, and replay it through native runtime execution before any

    failure is reported.'
  type: FR
- id: FR-024
  path: spec/replay/functional/FR-024-counterexample-envelope-intake.md
  role: context_only
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: When a counterexample is to be replayed, the code generator shall carry it to QSL as QSL's
  excerpt_start_line: 31
  excerpt: 'When a counterexample is to be replayed, the code generator shall carry it to QSL as QSL''s

    counterexample envelope (`qsl_replay::WitnessEnvelope`), keyed by QSL''s `ObligationIdentity` and

    holding exactly one `qsl_replay::ReplaySource` arm. It shall validate every value against its

    declared domain before any replay, and shall replay only through `qsl_replay::replay`, or through

    `qsl_replay::replay_frame` for a frame counterexample, or through

    `qsl_replay::replay_state_clause` for a postcondition state-clause counterexample.


    The envelope, the witness, the replay source, the FR-331 terminal reco'
  excerpt_kind: verbatim_prefix
  type: FR
- id: FR-032
  path: spec/replay/functional/FR-032-routed-scalar-replay-binding.md
  role: context_only
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: When the driver requests replay of a routed scalar counterexample, CG shall bind the request
  excerpt_start_line: 31
  excerpt: 'When the driver requests replay of a routed scalar counterexample, CG shall bind the request

    directly to its `ScalarObligationIdentity`, preserving the arithmetic-parity proposition the

    actual generated harness checked. This requirement owns a public request builder and a public

    settlement converter; the driver owns the intervening QSL replay call. QSL owns the operator-level

    exact evaluation, envelope arm, evidence and terminal causes.


    This is planned IR-631 work. The QSL operator and full-report identity contracts are merged and measured below.

    CG metadata retention, consumer conformance an'
  excerpt_kind: verbatim_prefix
  type: FR
- id: FR-033
  path: spec/replay/functional/FR-033-composite-parity-replay-binding.md
  role: context_only
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: 'Imported contexts remain PLANNED: the Eq constructor returns typed `ImportedContextUnsupported`'
  excerpt_start_line: 41
  excerpt: 'Imported contexts remain PLANNED: the Eq constructor returns typed `ImportedContextUnsupported`

    until CG retains admitted dependency packages from the original compile.


    When the driver submits a composite equality `bounded_shadow` item for settlement, CG shall

    construct a QSL-owned node-selected equality-parity claim over the original proving package. The

    proposition remains the independent equality verdict and admitted occurrence-pair count owned by

    [FR-015](../../kani/functional/FR-015-bounded-kani-obligations.md) AC-71 and the native refinement

    comparison owned by [FR-028](../../kani/funct'
  excerpt_kind: verbatim_prefix
  type: FR
- id: FR-019
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: context_only
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: When a backend provider envelope requests claims of this generator, the
  excerpt_start_line: 47
  excerpt: 'When a backend provider envelope requests claims of this generator, the

    generator shall settle each requested item at exactly one point, a `negotiate_*`

    arm over a closed backend kind, and shall settle no capability anywhere else.


    For production FR-330 consumption, the typed IR form and item accounting used

    by this arm come from the one admitted ContractPackage under

    [FR-039](../../core/functional/FR-039-contract-package-consumption.md).

    The original checked graph cannot override a package refusal or represented

    form.


    For a V2 scalar claim, form preflight is per driver item and per selected

    '
  excerpt_kind: verbatim_prefix
  type: FR
- id: FR-022
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-022-routed-generation.md
  role: context_only
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: When the orchestrating driver hands this generator the items that FR-019
  excerpt_start_line: 17
  excerpt: 'When the orchestrating driver hands this generator the items that FR-019

    settled `supported` and that QSL `route` then routed, each with its request

    index, its routed backend and that backend''s closed backend kind, together

    with one admitted IR `ContractPackageV1` and the complete lowering-position

    mapping, the generator shall run the

    generation arm of each item''s backend kind and return that arm''s output keyed

    by the item''s request index. It shall not settle, select or route a backend

    again.


    This is the CG generation arm of seam S9 (QSL ADR-012 §5 and §7.2 step 4;

    ADR-011 T-13 driver step 7 '
  excerpt_kind: verbatim_prefix
  type: FR
- id: FR-026
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-026-backend-adapter-contract.md
  role: context_only
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: The code generator shall hold everything specific to one linked proof backend in that backend's adap
  excerpt_start_line: 21
  excerpt: 'The code generator shall hold everything specific to one linked proof backend in that backend''s adapter,

    one implementation of a single adapter trait, and shall reach an adapter only through an exhaustive

    match on the closed `BackendKind` enum

    ([ADR-002](../../decisions/ADR-002-backend-adapter-boundary.md) Q0, Q1 and Q4). ADR-002 Q4 states how a

    second linked backend registers. `Process(BackendId)` has no CG adapter; the

    driver''s plugin host owns its process adapter (QSL ADR-029 PV-4).'
  type: FR
- id: FR-002
  path: spec/strategy/functional/FR-002-tristate-proptest.md
  role: context_only
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: When executable pre/post contracts are lowered, the generator shall emit entry-point harnesses and
  excerpt_start_line: 15
  excerpt: 'When executable pre/post contracts are lowered, the generator shall emit entry-point harnesses and

    proptest strategies that preserve pass, failed postcondition, and rejected precondition outcomes.'
  type: FR
- id: FR-008
  path: spec/strategy/functional/FR-008-bound-domain-strategy-admission.md
  role: context_only
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: For a request selecting one claim of an admitted `CheckedPackageV2`, the generator SHALL use Contrac
  excerpt_start_line: 21
  excerpt: 'For a request selecting one claim of an admitted `CheckedPackageV2`, the generator SHALL use Contract

    IR''s public clause-context integer-comparison operand accessor (IR FR-038-AC-202 through AC-209) to

    admit a direct comparison and derive its exact domains. The generator SHALL return one complete

    strategy bundle or one typed, located refusal; it SHALL NOT generate a partial bundle. This is the

    V2 input contract for the constructive population and campaign behavior of FR-009 through FR-012.

    The IR accessor and its public consumer test are implemented under IR-703 in Contract IR; IR''s

    fresh QSL '
  excerpt_kind: verbatim_prefix
  type: FR
- id: FR-009
  path: spec/strategy/functional/FR-009-constructive-correlated-populations.md
  role: context_only
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: When a selected claim of an admitted `CheckedPackageV2` is admitted by
  excerpt_start_line: 17
  excerpt: 'When a selected claim of an admitted `CheckedPackageV2` is admitted by

    [FR-008](./FR-008-bound-domain-strategy-admission.md), the generator shall emit proptest populations

    that construct every case directly inside the shared domain and on the requested side of the

    relation. A case is a complete valuation of the claim''s reads, including any `Post` read, and its tag

    is the value the selected claim''s V2 comparison oracle (FR-008) returns for that valuation. The

    generator never draws a candidate and then filters it out.'
  type: FR
- id: FR-010
  path: spec/strategy/functional/FR-010-domain-boundary-campaigns.md
  role: context_only
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: When a caller requests the `Boundary` population for a selected claim of a `CheckedPackageV2`
  excerpt_start_line: 17
  excerpt: 'When a caller requests the `Boundary` population for a selected claim of a `CheckedPackageV2`

    admitted by [FR-008](./FR-008-bound-domain-strategy-admission.md), the generator shall emit a finite,

    deterministic census of in-domain cases at the domain edges and the relation''s own edge. Every

    strategy bundle for a selected claim also carries the out-of-domain edge values, so a consumer can

    prove that it refuses them at domain admission. Each in-domain case is tagged with the value the

    selected claim''s V2 comparison oracle (FR-008) returns for it.'
  type: FR
- id: FR-011
  path: spec/strategy/functional/FR-011-numeric-harness-campaigns.md
  role: context_only
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: When a strategy bundle is generated for a selected claim of a `CheckedPackageV2`
  excerpt_start_line: 31
  excerpt: 'When a strategy bundle is generated for a selected claim of a `CheckedPackageV2`

    ([FR-008](./FR-008-bound-domain-strategy-admission.md)), the generator shall also emit an

    oracle-conformance campaign runner. The runner evaluates the selected claim''s V2 comparison oracle

    on each generated valuation, records the runtime verdict for the checked clause kind, and requires

    that verdict to equal the case''s

    expectation. Its summary reports the discard rate and the rejection rate as exact counts, or as

    unavailable when a counter may be saturated.


    The runner invokes no subject. A numeric subject harness'
  excerpt_kind: verbatim_prefix
  type: FR
- id: FR-012
  path: spec/strategy/functional/FR-012-constraint-preserving-shrinking.md
  role: context_only
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: When proptest shrinks a failing case drawn from a `Satisfying`, `Violating`, or `Broad` population o
  excerpt_start_line: 19
  excerpt: 'When proptest shrinks a failing case drawn from a `Satisfying`, `Violating`, or `Broad` population of

    a selected V2 claim ([FR-008](./FR-008-bound-domain-strategy-admission.md)), every candidate it visits shall stay inside
    the shared domain and keep the expectation tag

    of the case it came from. This refines [FR-002](./FR-002-tristate-proptest.md) FR-002-AC-4 for the

    populations of a selected V2 claim; FR-002-AC-4 itself stays verified by TC-004.'
  type: FR
- id: FR-013
  path: spec/strategy/functional/FR-013-it010-consumable-output.md
  role: context_only
  source_head: 1f49bed0469407016bb50f01d3e3c9732995df4e
  anchor: The generator shall deliver bound strategy, census, and runner output as typed generated Rust, so a
  excerpt_start_line: 21
  excerpt: 'The generator shall deliver bound strategy, census, and runner output as typed generated Rust, so a

    downstream crate can place every case''s values into its own runtime inputs by typed declaration identity, selected path
    and observation. The generator shall not

    require any serialized case format or schema owned by this repository for that consumption.'
  type: FR
